identity.industry: Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) & Mobile Value Chain

summary.oneLiner: Amber enters India's mobile-phone market — the world's 2nd largest — via an **asset-light sublease of an existing Oppo India facility** (covers Oppo, OnePlus, Realme of the BBK group), targeting ~8M units in Year 1 (FY28) and 13–15M in Year 2 (FY29). Initial EBITDA is thin (industry 1.5–2% ex-PLI) but the play is **scale + ROCE (>30–35% standalone, 4–10 day working capital) now, then backward integration** into HDI-PCBs and other components (where margins are 15–16%) over 5–6 years — explicitly modeled on how Amber added components to ACs over 25 years to reach ~70% BOM. Also diversifies revenue and cuts the seasonal concentration of the RAC business.

one-line thesis: Amber enters India's mobile-phone market — the world's 2nd largest — via an asset-light sublease of an existing Oppo India facility (covers Oppo, OnePlus, Realme of the BBK group), targeting ~8M units in Year 1 (FY28) and 13–15M in Year 2 (FY29). Initial EBITDA is thin (industry 1.5–2% ex-PLI) but the play is scale + ROCE (>30–35% standalone, 4–10 day working capital) now, then backward integration into HDI-PCBs and other components (where margins are 15–16%) over 5–6 years — explicitly modeled on how Amber added components to ACs over 25 years to reach ~70% BOM. Also diversifies revenue and cuts the seasonal concentration of the RAC business.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > No headline financials — this call was solely about the Oppo collaboration mechanics and roadmap.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Timeline: trial production Q4 FY27; commercial production Q1 FY28. First 3 months = learning curve (why the deliberately slow Q4FY27 start).
Volumes: ~8M units (management: 8–9M; take 8M conservatively) in Year 1 = FY28 → 13–15M units (14–15M conservative) in Year 2 = FY29. Represents ~20–30% of Oppo India's volume.
Margin: at commencement in line with industry (~1.5–2% EBITDA ex-PLI); improves as operating scale + local value addition rise.

Local value addition: start assembly + SMT (industry today only ~10–12%, "everybody doing only assembly"); add HDI PCBs in Year 2; then progressively raise local value addition to 35–40% over the next 5–6 years (mgmt also said "30–35%" — road map not yet formalized).
Capex: <₹50cr for assembly + SMT to start (asset-light sublease). Component-line capex only after 14–15M units is reached; PCB capex already underway (no duplication).
ROCE: mobile vertical >30–35% on a standalone basis; ROCE-accretive to group. PCB/component margins 15–16%.
order book & pipeline: Committed ramp: ~8M units Yr1 (FY28) → 13–15M units Yr2 (FY29), across 3 BBK brands (Oppo, OnePlus, Realme).
Long-term relationship framing — "beginning of a longer relationship with Oppo"; will explore additional avenues (incl. supplying components to Oppo/its other EMS partners over time).
Vivo: no arrangement. BBK-group brands beyond the three: not committed; "baby steps" first.
segment / subsidiary detail: Existing scale base (capability proof): IL JIN makes 9–10M smart watches/yr and ~15M PCB assemblies/yr; AC business does ~5.5M boxes/yr. Assembly scale "not a problem at all."

Ascent Circuits: Amber raised stake from 60% → 98.5%. Founder-MD Mr. Manjunath stepped down (no longer a shareholder). PCB division now headed by Mr. Santosh (25 yrs PCB experience, ex-AT&S — formerly the largest PCB company; with Amber ~1 year). "Amber has become the largest PCB company" with Ascent + Shogini.
Mobile entity structure undecided — will sit either directly under Amber or under IL JIN (IL JIN has minority shareholders on its cap table); decision before commencement of operations.
A dedicated senior-most management team will run the mobile vertical (separate from wearables/hearables).
growth verticals / optionality: Backward integration ladder: assembly + SMT → HDI interconnect PCBs (Yr2) → then one component every ~year (candidates named: camera modules, displays, metal casings, chargers) over 5–6 years.
Component margin pool (15–16% on PCB; "decent" across the mobile component ecosystem) is the real prize vs. thin assembly margins.
Oppo to help bring more component suppliers to India — ecosystem build-out for local value addition.

AC analogy as template: over 25 yrs Amber went sheet-metal → assembly → heat exchangers → injection molding → motor company → inverter PCB → fans & boards, reaching ~70% of BOM. Same "balance volume and value play" intended for mobile.
margins & cost dynamics: Assembly-only EBITDA structurally thin: industry ~1.5–2% ex-PLI; higher-end models ~1.5–1.7%, lower-end models a higher %.

Deal economics sit on the bottom line, not the top line — Amber has flexibility whether a model is booked gross (ODM-style) or on job-work value-add; absolute profit is protected either way (per Oppo India's choice, model by model).
Margin expansion is entirely a mix/value-addition story — SMT, then HDI/PCB (15–16%), then further components.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Assembly + SMT: <₹50cr total to start (sublease → no facility capex; "very, very minimal").
No Press Note 3 approval required (sublease of an existing Oppo facility) — removes a regulatory timeline risk.
Component capex deferred to after 14–15M units; magnitude depends on which components (camera modules / display / metal casings). PCB capex already in progress → no duplication.
On an "eventual investment" question (multiples of ₹1,000cr vs ₹200cr), mgmt declined a number — reiterated <₹50cr near-term and component capex sized later.
capital allocation: Asset-light, low-working-capital (4–5 days, max 10) → structurally high, improving ROCE (mobile >30–35% standalone).
Consistent with stated strategy: balance high-margin value-add businesses with asset-light, high-volume, low-margin businesses.
No equity dilution flagged for the initial phase; Ascent stake step-up (to 98.5%) already funded.
risks & watch-items: Execution / learning curve — ramping to ~8M units after a 3-month learning period; first commercial output only Q1FY28 (slippage risk).
Thin margins amplify any operational inefficiency; profitability hinges on the still-unformalized backward-integration road map landing on schedule.

Flat domestic phone TAM — total units sold in India roughly flat for 4–5 years; growth comes from ASP/premiumization and local-value-addition share, not unit growth. Amber "beats its TAM" within ~2 years at 15M, so the endless-TAM claim rests entirely on climbing the value chain.
PLI uncertainty — a revised (2nd) PLI is only speculated (value-addition-led); no draft yet; mgmt declined to model it.
Single-customer dependency on Oppo India volume stability; entity/accounting structure (gross vs job-work; Amber vs IL JIN) still undecided.
management quality / tone: Measured and disciplined — repeated "baby steps," a 3-month learning-curve buffer, and conservative volume framing (take 8M not 9M; 14–15M not "maybe more"). Credibility anchored in the demonstrated wearables scale-up (0→10M watches in ~4 years) and the 25-year AC backward-integration track record. Notably principled on ecosystem conduct: explicitly asked Oppo not to hand it other EMS players' existing business ("that is not Amber's model"). Declined to speculate on PLI structure or eventual capex numbers without hard data.
non-obvious takeaways: The sublease structure sidesteps Press Note 3 approval — a meaningful timeline/regulatory advantage over a fresh-facility entry.

Revenue-recognition is deliberately flexible (gross vs job-work) with protected absolute profit — so reported "revenue" from this vertical may be optically large or small without changing the P&L contribution; watch how it's disclosed.

Amber quietly consolidated to become "the largest PCB company" (Ascent 98.5% + Shogini) with an ex-AT&S leader — the PCB/HDI backbone that makes the mobile-component margin story credible pre-exists the Oppo deal.
Mgmt hints the relationship could invert over time — from Amber assembling Oppo phones to Amber supplying components to Oppo and even its other EMS partners.

qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q1FY27 (this — special update call): Oppo manufacturing collaboration signed 18-Jun-2026 (Oppo/OnePlus/Realme); asset-light sublease, no PN3; trial prod Q4FY27, commercial Q1FY28; 8M units FY28 → 13–15M FY29; local value-add 10–12% → 35–40% over 5–6 yrs (HDI in Yr2); capex <₹50cr to start; ROCE >30–35% standalone; Ascent stake 60%→98.5%, PCB div now under ex-AT&S Mr. Santosh.

Next Q → check: any Q1FY27 quarterly results (core AC/EMS numbers); facility/entity decision (Amber vs IL JIN; gross vs job-work); trial-production start on time (Q4FY27); PLI-2 draft; component capex sizing.

themes.title: Electronics manufacturing (EMS) & Make-in-India localization
themes.need: PLI + import-substitution + global China+1 sourcing drive an electronics-manufacturing build-out across consumer durables, defence and components. AMBER/PGEL/EPACK/SYRMA/AVALON/CYIENTDLM on box-build/EMS; DIXON-tier scale; CPPLUS/CNL on surveillance; KAYNES/SYRMA on integrated components; appliance ODMs (EPACK, AMBER) ride RAC/white-goods localization.
themes.driver: PLI disbursement + new ODM/OEM program wins; appliance season; defence/aero EMS conversion (AVALON, CYIENTDLM).
